To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HLA‐matched random‐donor platelet (PLT) transfusions are not associated with a significant reduction in mortality or in the frequency or severity of bleeding in patients with hypoproductive thrombocytosis.
there is no evidence to support the use of HLA‐matching in the transfusion of PLTs for patients with hypoprolyferative thrombocyanopenia.
HLA‐matched transfusion is associated with a reduction in mortality and in frequency of severe hemorrhage in patients with hypoproductive thrombocytosis.

the use of HLA‐matching to increase the efficacy of transfusions.
the development of an effective and efficient algorithm for determining the best HLA‐matched donors.
the development of new materials, the design and manufacture of new components, and the development of new processes.
